title: Density modes (comfortable and compact)
description: A system-level density setting that switches spacing, control heights, and table row heights between comfortable and compact through a small set of density tokens, so data-heavy users can see more rows without a separate component library. Type size stays readable in both modes.
intent: Let expert users trade whitespace for information density without degrading touch targets or readability.
characteristics: density tokens: control height, row height, inline and block padding
two modes, possibly three, never per-component ad hoc values
body text size unchanged or reduced at most one step
touch targets kept at 24px minimum (44px on touch-first surfaces)
interaction: Users switch density in settings or a table toolbar; the change applies immediately and persists.
responsive: Compact mode is ignored or limited on coarse-pointer devices (pointer: coarse) to keep touch targets usable.
accessibility: Target size meets WCAG 2.5.8 in both modes; text spacing overrides (WCAG 1.4.12) must not clip content in compact mode.
limitations: Doubles the visual QA matrix; test both modes in every state.
Not every component benefits; limit to tables, lists, and forms.
